land.text: Sijilmasa and the Tafilalt: 'In 976-7, Khazrun ibn Fulful ibn Khazar conquered Sijilmasa from the Banu Midrar'

predecessors.note: The Zenata held Fez before 979 (the page has them 'driven out of Fez and Sijilmasa' by Buluggin) but the page gives no date for Fez.

land.text: Fez and the north of Morocco: 'Varying sources date their capture of Fez to 1069 or some time later in the 1070s'; the Almoravids took Tlemcen 'towards 1080'

successors.note: The Sijilmasa page has the Almoravids kill the Maghrawa leader Mas'ud ibn Wanudin al-Maghrawi there 'in 1055'.

capitals.name: Sijilmasa
capitals.note: The page names no capital before Ziri; Sijilmasa is the first conquest and is entered for 976-986 as the principal city.

capitals.name: Fez
capitals.note: 'In 987-988 he was secure enough to be able to establish his court at Fes'.

capitals.name: Oujda
capitals.note: Ziri 'founded Oujda in 994 as his new capital'; the Ziri page says he 'built (or rebuilt)' it from August or September 994.

capitals.name: Fez
capitals.note: The page says Fez 'became Ziri ibn Atiyya's capital' and calls Tamim 'the last Maghrawa ruler of Fez'; it names no capital between 1002 and the Almoravid capture.

correction.text: Sijilmasa and the Tafilalt, conquered from the Banu Midrar

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area or frontier. Fez was Zenata land before 979 on the page's reading but the page does not date its capture, so only the Tafilalt is drawn.

correction.text: Sijilmasa and the Tafilalt, back in Zenata hands after the Zirid expedition of 979-983

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Between 979 and 983... briefly driven out of Fez and Sijilmasa'; the years 979-982 have no shape. The Zirid page of the sibling dossier has the Zirids abandon Morocco in 985.

correction.text: Sijilmasa and Fez, with 'supremacy in Fez by 987' and the title of amir of the Maghreb

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Ziri 'became master of the Maghreb in the year 991' but the page names no places beyond Fez, Oujda, Tiaret and Tlemcen. Fez is a 60 km circle, my reading.

correction.text: the Tafilalt, Oujda, Tiaret and Tlemcen, without Fez (taken by Abd al-Malik on 13 October 998)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. After the defeat near Tangier and the loss of Fez, Ziri 'fled to the Sahara, overthrew the remnants of the Idrisid dynasty at Tiaret, and expanded to include Tlemcen under Fatimid protection'; the year of the Tiaret and Tlemcen gains is not given (999 used).

correction.text: all of Ziri's former territories, restored to his son al-Mu'izz by al-Mansur: Fez, Sijilmasa, Oujda, Tiaret, Tlemcen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'He was succeeded by his son al-Mu'izz, who made his peace with al-Mansur, who restored him to possession of all his father's former territories.' The page names no later change of border until 1055; Banu Ifran took Fez in 1032-3 (Maghrawa page) and the Maghrawa page's Hammadid Buluggin took Fez from Futuh in 1062, neither with a recapture date.

correction.text: Fez, Oujda, Tiaret and Tlemcen, after the Almoravids killed the Maghrawa leader at Sijilmasa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1055' Abdallah ibn Yasin killed the Maghrawa leader Mas'ud ibn Wanudin al-Maghrawi at Sijilmasa; the Almoravids held it to 1146. The north is kept until the Almoravid capture of Fez, 'in 1069 or some time later in the 1070s'.

ledger.note: 976-7: the Maghrawa take Sijilmasa. 'In 976-7, Khazrun ibn Fulful ibn Khazar conquered Sijilmasa from the Banu Midrar' (the Sijilmasa page has the Midrarid dynasty fragment and fall to the Maghrawa without a date).
979: Buluggin ibn Ziri's expedition drives the Zenata out. 'Between 979 and 983, the Zenata were briefly driven out of Fez and Sijilmasa during a major expedition by Buluggin ibn Ziri.'
983: the Zenata return to Sijilmasa. The expedition of 979-983 ends and the Zenata, 'briefly driven out', are back; the sibling Zirid dossier has the Zirids abandon Morocco in 985.

987: Ziri ibn Atiyya takes Fez and is named amir of the Maghreb. 'In 987-988 he was secure enough to be able to establish his court at Fes after capturing it from the Idrisids'; the Maghrawa page: 'formally appointed amir of the Maghreb on behalf of the Umayyads in 987'.

region.text: Fes, taken 'by surprise in January 993' by Yaddu ibn Ya'la of the Banu Ifran

ledger.note: 993: the Banu Ifran take Fez. 'Yaddu ibn Ya'la took Fes by surprise in January 993 and held it for some months' (Banu Ifran page) while Ziri was in Cordoba; Ziri 'recaptured Fes in 993' (next event). Mirror of banu-ifran's 993 gain; added by reviewer af-02-x. Fez stays in the 987-997 keyframe because both moves fall in 993.

993: Ziri recaptures Fez from the Banu Ifran. Ziri 'recaptured Fes in 993 and displayed Yaddu's severed head on its walls'; Yaddu ibn Ya'la of the Banu Ifran had taken it while Ziri was in Cordoba (undated).
994: Ziri founds Oujda as his new capital. 'Ziri... founded Oujda in 994 as his new capital' (the Ziri page: built or rebuilt from August or September 994).

13 October 998: Fez opens its gates to Abd al-Malik. Almanzor's son defeated Ziri near Tangier; 'The inhabitants of Fes would not let him enter the city, but opened the gates to Abd al-Malik on October 13, 998.'

999 (bridge): Ziri takes Tiaret and Tlemcen. 'Ziri fled to the Sahara, overthrew the remnants of the Idrisid dynasty at Tiaret, and expanded to include Tlemcen under Fatimid protection'; the page gives no year after 998.

region.text: Fez and Oujda, his father's former territories

ledger.note: 1001: al-Mu'izz is restored to his father's lands. Ziri died on 5 August 1001 at Achir; his son 'made his peace with al-Mansur, who restored him to possession of all his father's former territories'.
1055: the Almoravids take Sijilmasa. 'According to al-Bakri, in 1055, Abdallah ibn Yasin killed the Maghrawa leader Mas'ud ibn Wanudin al-Maghrawi'; the Almoravids held the city until 1146.

region.text: Fez and the north of the Maghrawa lands

ledger.note: 1069-70: the Almoravids capture Fez and the last Maghrawa ruler Tamim is executed. 'Varying sources date their capture of Fez to 1069 or some time later in the 1070s'; the sibling Almoravid dossier gains Fez in 1070.

wars.name: Zirid expedition against the Zenata
wars.outcome: Buluggin ibn Ziri briefly drove the Zenata out of Fez and Sijilmasa between 979 and 983.

wars.name: Ziri ibn Atiyya against the Banu Ifran and the Umayyads
wars.outcome: Yaddu ibn Ya'la of the Banu Ifran took Fez while Ziri was in Cordoba; Ziri retook it in 993; in 996 al-Mansur cancelled his support; Abd al-Malik defeated him near Tangier and entered Fez on 13 October 998.
wars.note: The page does not date the Banu Ifran capture of Fez (between 991 and 993).

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the Maghrawa
wars.outcome: Sijilmasa fell in 1055 and Fez in 1069 or later in the 1070s; the Almoravids took Tlemcen 'towards 1080'; Tamim, the last Maghrawa ruler of Fez, was executed.

certainty.note: A tribal confederation's emirates: the pages name cities and no frontier; the 60 km circles are the researcher's.

notes: Cliopatria has no Maghrawa row. The pages opened do not give a founding of the 'state': the Maghrawa were the largest branch of the Zenata, and the dossier starts with Khazrun ibn Fulful's 976-7 conquest of Sijilmasa. The Maghrawa page has no infobox; 1070 is the Almoravid capture of Fez ('1069 or some time later in the 1070s'). The text calls Tamim 'the last Maghrawa ruler of Fez' while also giving the Banu Ifran leader Abu al-Kamal Tamim the capture of Fez in 1032-3 and the Hammadid Buluggin ibn Muhammad the expulsion of Futuh from Fez in 1062: the Fez timeline between 1001 and 1069 is not reconstructible from these pages (the sibling Hammadid dossier has the Hammama of Fez as a vassal 1039-1062) and the 1001-1054 keyframe keeps Fez throughout. Ziri's 'master of the Maghreb' (991) and 'amir of the Maghreb' (987) do not name territory. The Umayyad appointment of 987 and the Fatimid protection of Tlemcen after 998 are vassal-type relations recorded by the Caliphate of Cordoba and Fatimid dossiers if at all. Banu Ifran, Hammama and Idrisid remnants need their own dossiers (banu-ifran suggested). Gazetteer: Fez, Oujda, Tiaret, Tlimcen and Tafilalt resolve.
